ex_en: He hinted to me that he wants to get engaged
note: imperfect: نلمّح nlammi7 (I hint), يلمّح ylammi7 (he hints)

ex_en: The minister made a statement to the press
note: imperfect: نصرّح nSarri7 (I declare), يصرّح ySarri7 (he declares)

phrases.en: You have to declare the money at the airport
He declared his love to her

en: to make (someone) hate; to put off
ex_en: This teacher made me hate maths
note: imperfect: نكرّه nkarrih (I make hate), يكرّه ykarrih (he makes hate)

ex_en: My father made me love reading
note: imperfect: نحبّب n7abbib (I make like), يحبّب y7abbib (he makes like)

phrases.en: We need to make kids like school
May God make people love you

ex_en: I was surprised when I saw him
note: imperfect: نتفاجأ nitfāja' (I am surprised), يتفاجأ yitfāja' (he is surprised)

phrases.en: We were surprised by the news

ex_en: We surprised him with a party
note: imperfect: نفاجئ nfāji' (I surprise), يفاجئ yfāji' (he surprises)

phrases.en: I want to surprise my wife
He surprised me with his visit

ex_en: He let me down
note: imperfect: نخيّب nkhayyib (I disappoint), يخيّب ykhayyib (he disappoints)

phrases.en: May God never let your hopes down

en: to be moved; to be affected
ex_en: I was moved by his words
note: imperfect: نتأثّر nit'aththar (I am moved), يتأثّر yit'aththar (he is moved)

phrases.en: The crops were affected by the heat

ex_en: The news affected him deeply
note: imperfect: نأثّر naththir (I affect), يأثّر yaththir (he affects)

phrases.en: Staying up late affects your health

en: to get excited; to get enthusiastic
ex_en: He got excited about the idea
note: imperfect: نتحمّس nit7ammas (I get excited), يتحمّس yit7ammas (he gets excited)

phrases.en: The kids got excited about the trip

en: to repent; to give up (a bad habit)
ex_en: He gave up smoking for good
note: imperfect: نتوب ntūb (I repent), يتوب ytūb (he repents)

en: to rely on (God); to set off (trusting in God)
ex_en: Trust in God (and go ahead)
note: imperfect: نتوكّل nitwakkal (I rely on), يتوكّل yitwakkal (he relies on)

phrases.en: We put our trust in God and set off

en: to take precautions; to be on the safe side
ex_en: Be on the safe side and take an umbrella
note: imperfect: نحتاط ni7tāT (I take precautions), يحتاط yi7tāT (he takes precautions)

phrases.en: He kept some money aside just in case

en: to get ready; to prepare oneself
ex_en: Get ready for the exam
note: imperfect: نستعدّ nista3idd (I get ready), يستعدّ yista3idd (he gets ready)

en: to occur to; to cross one's mind
ex_en: An idea crossed my mind
note: imperfect: يخطر yukhTur (it occurs), يخطرلي yukhTurli (it occurs to me)

en: to mean; to intend; to head for
ex_en: What do you mean?
note: imperfect: نقصد nugSud (I mean), يقصد yugSud (he means)

phrases.en: We went to him for help with something

ex_en: He broke it on purpose
note: imperfect: نتعمّد nit3ammad (I do on purpose), يتعمّد yit3ammad (he does on purpose)

phrases.en: I swear I didn't do it on purpose

ex_en: He didn't dare tell him
note: imperfect: نتجرّأ nitjarra' (I dare), يتجرّأ yitjarra' (he dares)

phrases.en: I plucked up courage and asked him

en: to be lazy; to slack off
ex_en: Don't slack off
note: imperfect: نتكاسل nitkāsal (I am lazy), يتكاسل yitkāsal (he is lazy)

phrases.en: He got lazy and didn't finish the work
He's been lazing around since morning

en: to work hard; to make an effort
ex_en: Work hard so you pass
note: imperfect: نجتهد nijtihid (I work hard), يجتهد yijtihid (he works hard)

phrases.en: He worked very hard this year
I try as hard as I can

en: to free oneself up; to devote oneself (to)
ex_en: When I'm free I'll call you
note: imperfect: نتفرّغ nitfarragh (I free oneself up), يتفرّغ yitfarragh (he frees oneself up)

phrases.en: He devoted himself to his studies
I can't free myself up now

en: to get busy; to be preoccupied
ex_en: I got busy and didn't call
note: imperfect: ننشغل ninshghil (I get busy), ينشغل yinshghil (he gets busy)

phrases.en: He got caught up with work

ex_en: The matter is on my mind
note: imperfect: نشغل nushghul (I occupy), يشغل yushghul (he occupies)

phrases.en: He distracted me from my work

ex_en: Your son is stubborn, he doesn't listen.
note: f. عنيدة 3nīda; pl. عنيدين 3nīdīn. Libyans also say راسه قاسح (his head is hard).

ex_ar: الولد هذا قليل الأدب مع الناس الكبار.
ex_tr: il-weld hādha gallīl il-adab ma3 in-nās il-kbār.
ex_en: This boy is rude with older people.
note: f. قليلة الأدب gallīlt il-adab; pl. قليلين الأدب. Opposite of مربي.

ex_ar: خوك شجاع، ما يخافش من حد.
ex_en: Your brother is brave, he's afraid of nobody.
note: pl. شجعان shuj3ān. Libyan speech also uses راجل (a real man) for brave.

ex_en: Don't be a coward, go talk to him.
note: f. جبانة jbāna; pl. جبناء jubanā' / جبانين jbānīn.

phrases.en: that guy is a coward, he ran away

ex_en: Behave and I'll bring you a sweet.
note: f. عاقلة 3āgla; pl. عاقلين 3āglīn. Very common with children: كون عاقل "behave".

phrases.en: your daughter is so well-behaved, mashallah

ex_en: My brother knows a lot about electricity.
note: f. فاهمة fāhma; pl. فاهمين fāhmīn. Active participle used as adjective: انت فاهم؟ "do you get it?"

phrases.en: do you get what I mean?

ex_en: Our neighbour is a decent man.
note: f. محترمة mu7tarama; pl. محترمين mu7taramīn.

ex_en: Leave the money with him, he's trustworthy.
note: f. أمينة amīna; pl. أمناء umanā'.

phrases.en: he's not trustworthy, watch out for him

ex_en: He turned out to be a traitor and sold us out.
note: f. خاينة khāyna; pl. خونة khawana.

ex_ar: ما تكونش طماع، خذ نصيبك بس.
ex_tr: ma tkūnsh Tammā3, khudh nSībak bass.
ex_en: Don't be greedy, take only your share.
note: f. طماعة Tammā3a; pl. طماعين Tammā3īn.

phrases.en: the greedy man is never satisfied

ex_en: Don't tell her, she's envious.
note: f. حسودة 7asūda. Libyans fear the evil eye: عينه حارة "he has an envious eye".

ex_ar: من يوم صار مدير وهو متكبر.
ex_tr: min yōm Sār mudīr w huwwa mitkabbir.
ex_en: Since he became a manager he's been arrogant.
note: f. متكبرة mitkabbra; pl. متكبرين mitkabbrīn.

ex_ar: من يوم شرى الكرهبة وهو شايف روحه.
ex_tr: min yōm shra l-karhba w huwwa shāyif rū7ah.
ex_en: Since he bought the car he's been full of himself.
note: f. شايفة روحها shāyfa rū7ha; pl. شايفين رواحهم shāyfīn rwā7hum. Lit. "seeing himself".

phrases.en: you think you're better than us?

ex_en: Although he is rich, he is humble.
note: f. متواضعة mitwāD3a; pl. متواضعين mitwāD3īn.

ex_en: My mother is very patient with us.
note: f. صبورة Sabūra.

phrases.en: the teacher is patient with the kids

ex_en: My dad is a bit irritable in the morning.
note: f. عصبية 3aSabiyya; pl. عصبيين 3aSabiyyīn.

ex_en: The doctor is very gentle with the kids.
note: f. لطيفة laTīfa; pl. لطاف luTāf.

ex_en: Their daughter is modest and well brought-up.
note: f. حشيمة 7ashīma. Libyan praise for a decent, modest person, from حشمة.

phrases.en: a reserved man who doesn't talk much

ex_en: Your friend is so funny, we laughed a lot.
note: f. دمها خفيف dammha khfīf; pl. دمهم خفيف dammhum khfīf.

ex_ar: ما نحبش نقعد معاه، دمه ثقيل.
ex_tr: ma n7ibbsh nug3ud m3āh, dammah thgīl.
ex_en: I don't like sitting with him, he's unbearable.
note: f. دمها ثقيل dammha thgīl; pl. دمهم ثقيل dammhum thgīl.

ex_en: Are you serious or joking?
note: f. جدية jiddiyya; pl. جديين jiddiyyīn.

phrases.en: the teacher is very serious in class

ex_ar: الصغار هذول مؤدبين ما شاء الله.
ex_tr: iS-Sghār hadhōl mu'addabīn mā shā' allāh.
ex_en: These kids are well-mannered, mashallah.
note: f. مؤدبة mu'addaba; pl. مؤدبين mu'addabīn.

ex_ar: أختي منظمة، كل حاجة في بلاصتها.
ex_en: My sister is organized, everything is in its place.
note: f. منظمة munaDHDHama; pl. منظمين.

ex_en: This student neglects his studies.
note: f. مهملة muhmila; pl. مهملين muhmilīn.

ex_en: Your room is messy, tidy it up a bit.
note: f. فوضوية fawDawiyya.

ex_en: My friend is loyal, he never let me down.
note: f. مخلصة mukhliSa; pl. مخلصين mukhliSīn.

ex_en: The dog is loyal to its owner.
note: f. وفية wafiyya; pl. أوفياء awfiyā'.

ex_en: The wolf is cunning in folk tales.
note: f. مكارة makkāra; pl. مكارين makkārīn.

ex_en: His words are malicious, he means something by them.
note: f. خبيثة khabītha; pl. خبثاء khubathā'.

ex_en: The boy is innocent, he didn't do anything.
note: f. بريئة barī'a; pl. أبرياء abriyā'.

phrases.en: he was found innocent in court

ex_ar: هو على نيته، يصدق أي حد.
ex_en: He's naive, he believes anyone.
note: f. على نيتها 3la niyyt-ha; pl. على نياتهم 3la niyyāt-hum.

ex_en: He's hard-hearted, he shows no mercy.
note: f. قاسية gāsya; pl. قاسيين gāsyīn. (Different from قاسح "hard to the touch".)

ex_ar: جارتنا فضولية، تبي تعرف كل شي.
ex_tr: jāratna fuDūliyya, tibbi ta3rif kull shay.
ex_en: Our neighbour is nosy, she wants to know everything.
note: f. فضولية fuDūliyya; pl. فضوليين fuDūliyyīn.

ex_en: My aunt is so chatty, she never stops.
note: f. كثيرة الهدرة kthīrt il-hadra. From هدرز "to chat".

ex_en: My uncle is a level-headed man, people listen to him.
note: f. رزينة rzīna.

ex_en: He drives recklessly, he's going to cause an accident.
note: f. متهورة mitahawwra; pl. متهورين mitahawwrīn.

ex_ar: ولدي واعي، يعرف يقطع الشارع وحده.
ex_tr: weldi wā3i, ya3rif yigTa3 ish-shāri3 wa7dah.
ex_en: My son is careful, he can cross the street alone.
note: f. واعية wā3ya; pl. واعيين wā3yīn.

ex_ar: البايع هذا غشاش، ما تشريش منه.
ex_tr: il-bāyi3 hādha ghashshāsh, ma tishrīsh minnah.
ex_en: This seller is a cheat, don't buy from him.
note: f. غشاشة ghashshāsha; pl. غشاشين ghashshāshīn.

phrases.en: a student who cheats on exams

ex_tr: guddāmak yiD7ak w warāk yitkallam, munāfig.
ex_en: He smiles to your face and talks behind your back, a hypocrite.
note: f. منافقة munāfga; pl. منافقين munāfgīn.

ex_en: Their family is religious, they pray at the mosque.
note: f. متدينة mitdayyna; pl. متدينين mitdayynīn.

ex_en: An ambitious girl, she wants to become a doctor.
note: f. طموحة Tamū7a. Also a noun "ambition".

ex_en: Your son is diligent in his studies.
note: f. مجتهدة mujtahda; pl. مجتهدين mujtahdīn.

phrases.en: every hard worker gets his share (proverb)

ex_en: My sister is sociable, she loves people.
note: f. اجتماعية ijtimā3iyya. Also "social" as in social media (مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي).

phrases.en: he's not sociable, he likes to be alone

ex_en: Don't make fun of him, he's sensitive.
note: f. حساسة 7assāsa; pl. حساسين 7assāsīn. Also حساسية "allergy".

ex_ar: هي عاطفية هلبة، تبكي على أي حاجة.
ex_en: She's very emotional, she cries over anything.
note: f. عاطفية 3āTifiyya.

en: keen on; fond of; passionate about
ex_ar: خوي غاوي كورة، ما يفوتش ماتش.
ex_tr: khūy ghāwi kūra, ma yfawwitsh mātsh.
ex_en: My brother is crazy about football, he never misses a match.
note: f. غاوية ghāwya; pl. غاويين ghāwyīn. Followed directly by the thing: غاوي كورة.

ex_ar: الصغير مدلع، كل شي يبيه يجيبوهوله.
ex_tr: iS-Sghīr mdalla3, kull shay yibbih yjībūhūlah.
ex_en: The little one is spoiled, they get him everything he wants.
note: f. مدلعة mdall3a; pl. مدلعين mdall3īn.

ex_en: I'm optimistic, things will get better.
note: f. متفائلة mitfā'la.

ex_en: Why are you always pessimistic?
note: f. متشائمة mitshā'ma.

ex_en: I'm sure he'll come.
note: f. واثقة wāthga; pl. واثقين wāthgīn. واثق من روحه "self-confident".

ex_ar: راجل شهم، وقف معانا في الأزمة.
ex_tr: rājil shahm, wgif m3āna fi l-azma.
ex_en: A gallant man, he stood by us in the crisis.
note: pl. شهام shhām. High praise for a man who helps others.

ex_en: He left her on the street, a scoundrel.
note: pl. أنذال andhāl.

ex_tr: min yōm nja7 w huwwa maghrūr.
ex_en: Since he passed he's been conceited.
note: f. مغرورة maghrūra; pl. مغرورين.

phrases.en: a girl vain about her looks

ex_en: A trivial problem, it's not worth it.
note: f. تافهة tāfha; pl. تافهين tāfhīn.

ex_en: My grandfather is a wise man.
note: f. حكيمة 7akīma; pl. حكماء 7ukamā'. In some areas حكيم also means "doctor".

ex_en: Are you crazy? Driving at this speed!
note: f. مجنونة majnūna; pl. مجانين majānīn. Libyans also say مهبول (milder).

ex_en: You're responsible for your younger siblings.
note: f. مسؤولة mas'ūla; pl. مسؤولين mas'ūlīn. Also a noun "official".

ex_tr: iS-Sghīr gāfiz, yifhamha w hiyya Tāyra.
ex_en: The little one is sharp, he gets it immediately.
note: f. قافزة gāfza; pl. قافزين gāfzīn. Typically Libyan; also used ironically for a smart-alec.

phrases.en: a girl who's sharp at maths

ex_en: He's good at business.
note: f. فالحة fāl7a. Often sarcastic: فالح غير في الأكل "good only at eating".

phrases.en: a girl who's capable at everything

ex_en: He spoke to him politely.
note: f. مهذبة muhadhdhaba; pl. مهذبين.

ex_ar: الصغير بكاي، يبكي على أي حاجة.
ex_en: The little one is a crybaby, he cries over anything.
note: f. بكاية bakkāya.

phrases.en: a girl who cries a lot

ex_en: He's always grumpy, he never laughs.
note: f. نكدية nakadiyya.

phrases.en: don't be a killjoy at the wedding

ex_en: Come in, don't be shy.
note: f. مستحية mista7ya; pl. مستحيين mista7yīn.

phrases.en: the little girl is shy with the guests
I'm too shy to tell him

ex_en: A bold question, but fine.
note: f. جريئة jarī'a.

ex_en: My dad is careful with money.
note: f. حريصة 7arīSa; pl. حريصين 7arīSīn.

ex_en: His wife is a spendthrift, she spends everything.
note: f. مبذرة mbadhdhra.

ex_en: My mum is forgiving, she forgets quickly.
note: f. متسامحة mitsām7a; pl. متسامحين.

ex_ar: ما تكونش أناني، قسم مع خوك.
ex_tr: ma tkūnsh anāni, gassim ma3 khūk.
ex_en: Don't be selfish, share with your brother.
note: f. أنانية anāniyya; pl. أنانيين.

ex_en: Don't hold a grudge, forgive him.
note: f. حقودة 7agūda.

ex_en: This noise is very annoying.
note: f. مزعجة muz3ja.

ex_en: A cheerful girl, always smiling.
note: f. ضحوكة Da7ūka.

ex_en: Why are you frowning today?
note: f. مكشرة mkashshra.

phrases.en: he always has a sour face

ex_en: He's not dull, he just doesn't study.
note: f. بليدة blīda.

ex_en: My uncle is cultured, he reads lots of books.
note: f. مثقفة muthaqqafa; pl. مثقفين.

ex_en: His mother is educated and works.
note: f. متعلمة mit3allma; pl. متعلمين.

ex_en: My grandmother is illiterate, she can't read.
note: f. أمية ummiyya; pl. أميين. Do not confuse with أمي "my mother".

ex_en: In the film this man is the villain.
note: f. شريرة sharrīra; pl. شريرين.

ex_en: Smoking is harmful to health.
note: f. مؤذية mu'dhya.

ex_en: Our neighbour is helpful, he helps everyone.
note: f. خدومة khadūma.

ex_en: The employee was arrogant with us.
note: f. متعجرفة mit3ajrfa.

ex_en: People here are friendly.
note: f. ودودة wadūda.

ex_en: To be frank with you, I didn't like it.
note: f. صريحة Sarī7a. نكون صريح معاك "to be honest with you".

ex_en: Quiet, the baby is asleep.
note: f. نايمة nāyma; pl. نايمين nāymīn. Libyans also say راقد.

ex_en: My dad is asleep, don't shout.
note: f. راقدة rāgda; pl. راقدين rāgdīn. Libyan رقد "to sleep".

phrases.en: I found him asleep on the sofa

ex_en: Have you been awake since early?
note: f. فايقة fāyga; pl. فايقين fāygīn. Libyan فاق "to wake up".

ex_en: He was driving drunk.
note: f. سكرانة sakrāna; pl. سكارى sakāra.

ex_en: He's sick, he's not fasting today.
note: f. فاطرة fāTra; pl. فاطرين fāTrīn.

ex_en: His wife is seven months pregnant.
note: pl. حوامل 7awāmil. Only feminine in sense (مرته حامل).

ex_ar: خوي الكبير معرس وعنده زوز صغار.
ex_tr: khūy il-kbīr m3arris w 3andah zūz Sghār.
ex_en: My older brother is married with two kids.
note: f. معرسة m3arrsa; pl. معرسين m3arrsīn. Libyan, from عرّس "to marry". Also متزوج mitzawwij.

ex_en: She's been married for five years.
note: f. متزوجة mitzawwja; pl. متزوجين mitzawwjīn.

ex_en: He's still single, he hasn't married.
note: f. عازبة 3āzba; pl. عزاب 3uzzāb.

ex_en: She's divorced and has a daughter.
note: f. مطلقة mTallga; pl. مطلقين mTallgīn.

ex_en: My grandfather has been a widower for a long time.
note: f. أرملة armla; pl. أرامل arāmil.

ex_en: My sister is engaged, the wedding is in summer.
note: f. مخطوبة makhTūba. Usually said of the woman.

en: unemployed; out of work; broken down
ex_en: My cousin has been unemployed for a year.
note: f. عاطلة 3āTla; pl. عاطلين 3āTlīn.

phrases.en: the machine is out of order

ex_en: The teacher is absent today.
note: f. غايبة ghāyba; pl. غايبين ghāybīn.

phrases.en: away from home for a week

ex_en: All the students are present.
note: f. حاضرة 7āDra; pl. حاضرين 7āDrīn. As a reply to a request: حاضر "right away".

ex_en: Is Mohammed in? — No, he went out.
note: f. موجودة mawjūda; pl. موجودين mawjūdīn. Very common: موجود؟ "is he in?"

phrases.en: bread is available at the bakery

ex_en: I'm willing to help you.
note: f. مستعدة mista3idda; pl. مستعدين mista3iddīn.

ex_en: The key is lost, I can't find it.
note: f. ضايعة Dāy3a; pl. ضايعين Dāy3īn.

ex_en: We were lost on the road for an hour.
note: f. تايهة tāyha; pl. تايهين tāyhīn.

phrases.en: lost, doesn't know where he's going

ex_en: Our neighbours' son has been locked up for a month.
note: f. محبوسة ma7būsa; pl. محبوسين ma7būsīn.

phrases.en: the cat is shut in the room

ex_en: Is the AC on?
note: f. شغالة shaghghāla. Libyan: الكهربا شغالة "the power is on".

ex_en: The light is off, I can't see.
note: f. طافية Tāfya. Libyan: الضي طافي "the light is off".

phrases.en: the power has been off since the morning

ex_en: I left the light on in the room.
note: f. شاعلة shā3la. Libyan: الضي شاعل "the light is on".

ex_en: I can't stay, I'm in a hurry.
note: f. مزروبة mazrūba; pl. مزروبين mazrūbīn. Very Libyan, from زرب "to hurry".

phrases.en: why are you in such a rush?

ex_en: The matter is closed, that's it.
note: f. منتهية mintihya.

ex_en: The bill is settled, you owe nothing.
note: f. خالصة khālSa. Also used as an adverb "at all" (مش باهي خالص).

phrases.en: the rent is paid for this month

ex_en: Entry is free for children.
note: f. مجانية majjāniyya. Libyans also say بلاش.

ex_en: She's taken, she has a fiancé.
note: f. مرتبطة mirtabTa.

ex_tr: būy aSla3 min w huwwa Sghīr.
ex_en: My dad has been bald since he was young.
note: f. صلعة Sal3a; pl. صلع Sul3. Libyans also say راسه أملس.

phrases.en: a bald man with a beard

ex_en: Her hair is curly and long.
note: f. مجعدة mja33da.

phrases.en: the shirt is creased, iron it

ex_en: His hair is soft as silk.
note: f. ناعمة nā3ma; pl. ناعمين.

ex_en: He became skinny after the illness.
note: f. نحيفة n7īfa; pl. نحاف n7āf.

phrases.en: you need to eat, you're skinny

ex_en: This man is huge, as big as a door.
note: f. ضخمة Dakhma; pl. ضخام Dkhām.

ex_en: Her groom is handsome and decent.
note: pl. وسيمين wasīmīn. Libyans more often say زين or مزيان for looks.

ex_ar: جدي ولى أعمى في آخر عمره.
ex_en: My grandfather went blind late in life.
note: f. عميا 3amya; pl. عميان 3umyān.

phrases.en: are you blind? didn't you see it?

ex_en: Speak loudly, my grandad is a bit deaf.
note: f. طرشا Tarsha; pl. طرش Tursh.

ex_en: Our neighbours' son is mute, he speaks with signs.
note: f. خرسا kharsa; pl. خرس khurs.

phrases.en: he went silent like a mute
don't just sit there silent, speak

ex_en: He's been limping since the accident.
note: f. عرجا 3arja.

ex_en: The little one is a bit cross-eyed, he needs glasses.
note: f. حولا 7awla.

phrases.en: he's not cross-eyed, he's winking at you

ex_en: The pirate is one-eyed in the film.
note: f. عورا 3awra.

phrases.en: in the land of the blind the one-eyed man is king

ex_en: My son is left-handed, he writes with his left.
note: f. عسرا 3asra.

ex_ar: أختي متحجبة من وهي في الإعدادي.
ex_tr: ukhti mit7ajjba min w hiyya fi l-i3dādi.
ex_en: My sister has worn the hijab since middle school.
note: Feminine only; pl. متحجبات mit7ajjbāt. Also محجبة m7ajjba.

ex_en: You're dressed smart today, where are you off to?
note: Invariable (French chic). Very common in Libya.

ex_en: Her father is always an elegant man.
note: f. أنيقة anīga; pl. أنيقين.

ex_en: The room is tidy and clean.
note: f. مرتبة mrattba. Note: as a noun مرتّب also means "salary".

ex_en: The kitchen is cluttered, there are lots of dishes.
note: f. مكركبة mkarkba. Common Libyan for a cluttered place.

ex_ar: يمشي للجيم كل يوم، ولى معضل.
ex_tr: yimshi l-il-jīm kull yōm, walla m3aDDal.
ex_en: He goes to the gym every day, he's got buff.
note: f. معضلة m3aDDla. Libyan/Arabic slang from عضلة.

ex_en: My uncle is pot-bellied from eating.
note: f. مكرشة mkarrsha. From كرش "belly".

phrases.en: he got a belly after the wedding

ex_en: He came back from the beach tanned.
note: f. مسمرة msammra. From أسمر "brown".

phrases.en: his face is tanned from the sun

ex_en: Your face is pale, are you sick?
note: f. باهتة bāhta.

phrases.en: the shirt has faded from washing

ex_en: That bearded man is our neighbour.
note: pl. ملتحيين milti7yīn. Also بلحية b-li7ya "with a beard".

ex_en: The car is fixed, you can take it.
note: f. مصلحة mSall7a. From صلّح "to fix".

phrases.en: the phone is repaired and works

en: broken down; out of order; delayed
ex_en: The lift is out of order, take the stairs.
note: f. معطلة m3aTTla.

phrases.en: the car broke down on the road

ex_en: The kids left the toy broken.
note: f. مخربة mkharrba. From خرّب "to break/ruin".

phrases.en: the road is ruined, all potholes
the house is damaged from the war

ex_en: This meat is spoiled, throw it away.
note: f. فاسدة fāsda; pl. فاسدين fāsdīn.

ex_en: The bread is mouldy, it has green on it.
note: f. معفنة m3affna.

ex_en: This fish is rotten, it smells bad.
note: f. خامجة khāmja. Libyan word for bad-smelling, gone-off things; also an insult.

ex_en: This watch is fake, not original.
note: f. مزيفة mzayyfa. Libyans also say تقليد for knock-off goods.

ex_en: These trainers are knock-offs, they're cheap.
note: Used like an adjective after a noun: شنطة تقليد "a knock-off bag".

ex_en: The market is crowded today, Thursday.
note: f. مزحومة maz7ūma. From زحمة.

ex_en: This sofa is very comfortable.
note: f. مريحة murī7a. (Of people: مرتاح.)

ex_en: Travelling by car is tiring.
note: f. متعبة mut3ba. (Of people: تعبان.)

ex_en: This book is very useful.
note: f. مفيدة mufīda.

ex_en: Too much sugar is harmful.
note: f. ضارة Dārra.

ex_en: This film is boring, I fell asleep.
note: f. مملة mumilla. Libyans also say يقلّق "it's boring".

ex_en: The trip was very enjoyable.
note: f. ممتعة mumti3a.

ex_en: The view is wonderful from up there.
note: f. رائعة rā'i3a. More formal than هايل.

ex_en: The traffic today is terrible.
note: f. فظيعة faDHī3a. Like English "awesome/awful", context decides.

phrases.en: the food is amazing, bless your hands

ex_en: The road is scary at night.
note: f. مخيفة mukhīfa.

ex_ar: الحي هذا آمن، ما فيهش مشاكل.
ex_tr: il-7ayy hādha āmin, ma fīhsh mashākil.
ex_en: This neighbourhood is safe, there's no trouble.
note: f. آمنة āmna.

phrases.en: the road isn't safe at night

ex_en: This job is a sure thing, don't worry.
note: f. مضمونة maDmūna.

ex_en: It's impossible to get there in an hour.
note: Also used alone as an exclamation: مستحيل! "no way!".

phrases.en: no way! I don't believe it

ex_en: You must come tomorrow.
note: f. ضرورية Darūriyya. ضروري تجي "you must come".

ex_en: Is the food enough for everyone?
note: f. كافية kāfya. Libyans often say يكفي or بزايد.

ex_en: Is there an extra chair?
note: f. زايدة zāyda. Also "plus" in arithmetic.

phrases.en: there's a bit too much salt

ex_en: He has a private driver.
note: f. خاصة khāSSa. Also خاص بـ "specific to".

ex_en: The public hospital is crowded.
note: f. عامة 3āmma. (Distinct from عام "year".)

ex_en: The official holiday is on Thursday.
note: f. رسمية rasmiyya.

ex_en: This is a personal question.
note: f. شخصية shakhSiyya. Also "in person": شخصيا.

ex_en: These tomatoes are local, not imported.
note: f. محلية ma7alliyya.

ex_en: A hundred percent natural honey.
note: f. طبيعية Tabī3iyya. طبيعي! "of course!"

ex_en: This grass is artificial, not natural.
note: f. صناعية Sinā3iyya.

ex_en: This shop is well known in Tripoli.
note: f. معروفة ma3rūfa. Also as noun "a favour".

ex_en: This number is unknown, I don't recognise it.
note: f. مجهولة majhūla.

ex_en: My siblings are very different from each other.
note: f. مختلفة mukhtalfa; pl. مختلفين.

ex_en: Your son looks a lot like you.
note: f. شبيهة shbīha. Libyans often say يشبه or زي.

ex_en: Now isn't a good time.
note: f. مناسبة munāsba.

phrases.en: an outfit suitable for the wedding

ex_en: The passport is valid until next year.
note: f. صالحة Sāl7a.

phrases.en: the water isn't fit to drink

ex_en: This isn't legal.
note: f. قانونية gānūniyya.

ex_en: Most things in the market are imported.
note: f. مستوردة mustawrada.

ex_en: Is the clock right?
note: f. مظبوطة maDbūTa. Also "exactly!" as a reply.

ex_en: You must be precise in the accounts.
note: f. دقيقة dagīga. (Homograph of دقيق "flour".)

ex_ar: راجل غامض، ما يحكيش على روحه.
ex_en: A mysterious man, he doesn't talk about himself.
note: f. غامضة ghāmDa.

phrases.en: the matter is a bit unclear

ex_en: Is the lesson clear?
note: Also used as "got it!": مفهوم.

ex_en: The paperwork at the municipality is complicated.
note: f. معقدة m3agda.

ex_en: A small problem, it'll be solved.
note: f. بسيطة basīTa; pl. بسطاء busaTā'. بسيطة! "no big deal!"

ex_en: This hotel is luxurious, very expensive.
note: f. فاخرة fākhra.

ex_en: We love Libyan home-style food.
note: f. شعبية sha3biyya.

ex_en: She wore the traditional outfit at the wedding.
note: f. تقليدية taglīdiyya.

ex_en: A modern building downtown.
note: f. حديثة 7adītha. (Also noun "conversation; hadith".)

ex_en: My aunt wears modern clothes.
note: f. عصرية 3aSriyya.

ex_en: This stamp is very rare.
note: f. نادرة nādra. نادرا "rarely".

ex_en: This illness is widespread in winter.
note: f. منتشرة mintashra.

ex_en: You're wearing the shirt inside out!
note: f. مقلوبة maglūba.

phrases.en: an overturned car on the road

ex_en: The picture is crooked, straighten it.
note: f. معوجة m3awwja.

ex_en: Go straight and then turn right.
note: Invariable in Libyan speech. Also امشي عدل "go straight".

ex_en: The pole is leaning a bit.
note: f. مايلة māyla.

ex_en: The ground here is level.
note: f. مستوية mistwya. In Libyan the "cooked" sense is very common (اللحم مستوي؟).

phrases.en: is the meat cooked or not?

ex_en: An oval mirror in the bathroom.
note: f. بيضاوية bayDāwiyya. From بيضة "egg".

ex_en: Careful, the knife is sharp.
note: f. حادة 7ādda.

ex_ar: السكينة هذي ماضية، اقطع بيها اللحم.
ex_tr: is-sikkīna hādhi māDya, igTa3 bīha l-la7am.
ex_en: This knife is sharp, cut the meat with it.
note: f. ماضية māDya. Libyan for a sharp knife; opposite مش ماضي "blunt".

ex_en: His hands are rough from work.
note: f. خشنة khshina.

ex_ar: الجو رطب في طرابلس في الصيف.
ex_tr: il-jaw raTb fi Trābulus fi S-Sēf.
ex_en: The weather is humid in Tripoli in summer.
note: f. رطبة raTba. The humidity: الرطوبة.

ex_en: Drink lukewarm water in the morning.
note: f. فاترة fātra.

phrases.en: the tea is lukewarm, heat it up

ex_en: The chicken is frozen, let it thaw.
note: f. مجمدة mjammda.

ex_ar: نبي مشروب مثلج في السخانة هذي.
ex_tr: nibbi mashrūb mthallij fi s-skhāna hādhi.
ex_en: I want an ice-cold drink in this heat.
note: f. مثلجة mthallja.

ex_en: Bazin is a rich, heavy dish.
note: f. دسمة dasma.

ex_en: The couscous is delicious, bless your hands.
note: f. لذيذة ldhīdha. Libyans also say بنين for tasty.

ex_en: My brother is two years older than me.
note: Elative of كبير. Invariable in Libyan speech (no feminine كبرى except in set phrases). Superlative: أكبر واحد "the biggest one".

ex_en: My sister is younger than me.
note: Elative of صغير. Invariable.

ex_en: The coffee here is better than over there.
note: Elative of باهي/حسن. Very common: أحسن حاجة "the best thing"; أحسن! "good, serves him right!".

phrases.en: best thing is we sleep early

ex_en: This road is worse than the first.
note: Libyan elative of خايب "bad". Invariable.

phrases.en: the worst day of my life

ex_en: Your son has become taller than you.
note: Elative of طويل.

phrases.en: the tallest man on the team

ex_en: Take the shorter road.
note: Elative of قصير.

ex_en: Gold has become more expensive than before.
note: Elative of غالي. Also "dearest": أغلى ناس "dearest people".

ex_en: The popular market is cheaper than the mall.
note: Elative of رخيص.

ex_en: By plane is faster than by road.
note: Elative of سريع.

ex_en: This bag is heavier than the other.
note: Elative of ثقيل.

phrases.en: the heaviest thing in the house
he's even more annoying than his dad

ex_en: Take the lighter bag.
note: Elative of خفيف. أخف الضررين "the lesser evil".

ex_ar: الامتحان هذا أسهل من اللي فات.
ex_tr: il-imti7ān hādha as-hal min illi fāt.
ex_en: This exam is easier than the last one.
note: Elative of ساهل/سهل.

ex_en: Maths is my hardest subject.
note: Elative of صعيب.

ex_en: Where's the nearest pharmacy?
note: Elative of قريب.

ex_en: The new house is farther from work.
note: Elative of بعيد.

ex_en: The world is nicer in spring.
note: Elative of حلو.

ex_en: This colour suits you better.
note: Libyan elative of زين. Invariable.

phrases.en: the most beautiful country in the world

ex_en: This coffee is stronger than usual.
note: Elative of قوي.

phrases.en: the strongest team in the league

ex_en: The signal is weaker here.
note: Elative of ضعيف.

phrases.en: he got weaker after the illness

ex_ar: الجامع هذا أقدم جامع في المدينة.
ex_tr: ij-jāmi3 hādha agdam jāmi3 fi l-mdīna.
ex_en: This mosque is the oldest in the old city.
note: Elative of قديم.

ex_en: Do you have a newer model?
note: Elative of جديد. Also آخر موديل "latest model".

phrases.en: the newest thing on the market

ex_en: The sea is cleaner here.
note: Elative of نظيف.

phrases.en: the cleanest restaurant in the area

ex_en: Today is hotter than yesterday.
note: Elative of سخون.

phrases.en: the hottest month of the year

ex_en: Tonight is colder than last night.
note: Elative of بارد.

phrases.en: the coolest spot in the house
the mountains are colder than the coast

ex_en: Health is more important than money.
note: Elative of مهم. المهم "the main thing".

phrases.en: nothing is more important than family

ex_en: It's better that you go early.
note: Slightly more formal synonym of أحسن.

ex_en: This is the worst decision I've made.
note: Formal-ish; Libyans often say أخيب.

ex_en: My sister is the smartest in the class.
note: Elative of ذكي.

ex_en: He's the richest man in the area.
note: Elative of غني.

phrases.en: the richest people in the country

ex_ar: العيلة هذي أفقر عيلة في الحي.
ex_en: This family is the poorest in the neighbourhood.
note: Elative of فقير.

ex_en: The tallest building in Tripoli.
note: Elative of عالي.

ex_en: Turn the volume down, make it lower.
note: Libyan elative of واطي.

ex_en: This room is roomier than the first.
note: Elative of واسع.

ex_en: This alley is narrower.
note: Elative of ضيق.

ex_en: He's the best at maths.
note: Elative of شاطر.

phrases.en: the best cook in the family

ex_en: My mum is the kindest person in the world.
note: Elative of طيب.

ex_en: Tripoli is more beautiful at night.
note: Elative of جميل.

phrases.en: the most beautiful day of my life

en: more dangerous; most dangerous; more serious
ex_en: The coastal road is more dangerous at night.
note: Elative of خطير.

phrases.en: the matter is more serious than that

ex_en: The internet is slower than usual today.
note: Elative of بطيء.

ex_en: The most famous Libyan dish is bazin.
note: Elative of مشهور.

ex_en: Home food is healthier.
note: Elative of صحيح. الأصح "the correct way".

phrases.en: it's more correct to say it this way

ex_en: The kids are having fun at the beach.
note: f. مستانسة mistānsa; pl. مستانسين mistānsīn. Very common Libyan; from استانس "to enjoy oneself".

phrases.en: are you having a good time here?

ex_ar: حاسس روحي مخنوق في الحوش، نبي نطلع.
ex_tr: 7āsis rū7i makhnūg fi l-7ōsh, nibbi nuTla3.
ex_en: I feel stifled at home, I want to go out.
note: f. مخنوقة makhnūga. Libyan: حاسس روحي مخنوق "I feel suffocated (emotionally)".

ex_en: I regret what I did.
note: f. ندمانة nadmāna; pl. ندمانين.

ex_en: He was too embarrassed to ask.
note: f. مكسوفة maksūfa. Libyans also say محشوم.

phrases.en: her face went red, she's embarrassed

ex_en: We're all shocked by the news.
note: f. مصدومة maSdūma; pl. مصدومين.

ex_en: The little one is terrified of the dog.
note: f. مرعوبة mar3ūba.

ex_en: Now I'm reassured, you arrived safely.
note: f. مطمنة mTammna. Libyan form of مطمئن.

phrases.en: I don't feel good about this man

ex_en: I'm not interested in politics.
note: f. مهتمة muhtamma.

phrases.en: he takes care of his health

ex_en: I feel frustrated with work.
note: f. محبطة mu7baTa.

ex_en: I'm looking forward to seeing you.
note: f. متشوقة mitshawwga.

ex_en: I'm hesitant whether to go or not.
note: f. مترددة mitraddda.

ex_en: I was embarrassed in front of people.
note: f. محرجة mu7raja. (محرِج mu7rij = embarrassing.)

phrases.en: don't put me in an awkward spot

ex_en: We're all affected by this news.
note: f. متأثرة mit'aththra.

phrases.en: deeply affected by his grandfather's death

ex_en: Why are you irritated? What happened?
note: f. متنرفزة mitnarfza. From French nerf; very common in Libya.

ex_en: He lives carefree, without worries.
note: f. متهنية mithannya. Libyan: نوم متهني "sound sleep".

en: in a great mood; buzzing; enjoying
ex_en: With my morning coffee I'm in a great mood.
note: f. مكيفة mkayyfa. Libyan slang from كيف "pleasure". (Homograph of مكيّف "air conditioner".)

phrases.en: you look in a great mood today

ex_en: Don't talk to her now, she's upset.
note: f. مشوشة mshawwsha. Libyan: مشوش = upset/bothered.

ex_ar: ما تكونش يائس، كل شي يتحل.
ex_tr: ma tkūnsh yā'is, kull shay yit7all.
ex_en: Don't despair, everything gets solved.
note: f. يائسة yā'sa.

ex_ar: عيد سعيد وكل عام وانتم بخير.
ex_tr: 3īd sa3īd w kull 3ām w intum b-khēr.
ex_en: Happy Eid, and many happy returns.
note: f. سعيدة sa3īda. Common in wishes: عيد سعيد "happy Eid", يوم سعيد.

ex_en: I'm impressed by the way you work.
note: f. معجبة mu3jaba; pl. معجبين. معجب بيها "he fancies her".

ex_en: He was amazed by the view.
note: f. مبهورة mabhūra.

ex_en: My grandma is in pain from her knee.
note: f. متألمة mit'allma.

ex_en: People are sympathetic to the family.
note: f. متعاطفة mit3āTfa.

ex_en: My dad is angry with me.
note: f. غضبانة ghaDbāna. More formal than متغشش; also used of God or parents' displeasure.

ex_ar: لما نجح كان طاير من الفرحة.
ex_tr: lamma nja7 kān Tāyir min il-far7a.
ex_en: When he passed he was over the moon.
note: f. طايرة من الفرحة Tāyra min il-far7a.

ex_en: I'm upset over the missed opportunity.
note: f. متقهرة mitgahhra. Libyan, related to مقهور.

ex_en: He was flustered in the interview.
note: f. مرتبكة mirtabka.

ex_en: I'm not convinced by what you say.
note: f. مقتنعة mugtin3a.

ex_en: Are you sure the shop is open?
note: f. متأكدة mit'akkda; pl. متأكدين mit'akkdīn. Very common: متأكد؟ "are you sure?".

ex_en: Do you need anything from the market?
note: f. محتاجة mi7tāja; pl. محتاجين mi7tājīn. محتاج حاجة؟ "do you need anything?".

ex_ar: مش قادر نمشي، رجلي توجع فيا.
ex_tr: mush gādir nimshi, rijli twajja3 fiyya.
ex_en: I can't walk, my leg hurts.
note: f. قادرة gādra; pl. قادرين gādrīn. Libyans more often use نقدر "I can" but قادر is common too.

ex_en: Her father agrees to the marriage.
note: f. موافقة mwāfga; pl. موافقين mwāfgīn. As a reply: موافق "agreed".

ex_en: I'm used to waking up early.
note: f. متعودة mit3awda; pl. متعودين mit3awdīn. متعود على "used to".

ex_en: Why are you standing? Sit down.
note: f. واقفة wāgfa; pl. واقفين wāgfīn.

phrases.en: the car is parked in front of the house
work has come to a halt

ex_en: I have to go now.
note: f. مضطرة muDTarra. مش مضطر "you don't have to".

phrases.en: we were forced to sell the car

ex_en: I'm forced to work on Friday.
note: f. مجبورة majbūra.

ex_en: I'm waiting for you in front of the door.
note: f. مستنية mistannya; pl. مستنيين. From استنى "to wait".

phrases.en: I sat waiting for an hour

en: staying up late; awake at night
ex_en: We stayed up until dawn.
note: f. سهرانة sahrāna; pl. سهرانين.

en: on the way home; heading home
ex_en: I'm heading home, do you want anything?
note: f. مروحة mraww7a; pl. مروحين mraww7īn. From روّح "to go home".

phrases.en: I found him on his way home

ex_en: The little one runs around the house naked.
note: f. عريانة 3iryāna; pl. عريانين.

phrases.ar: حاسس روحي عريان من غير تلفون
phrases.en: I feel naked without my phone

ex_en: Don't walk barefoot, the floor is cold.
note: f. حافية 7āfya; pl. حفيانين 7afyānīn.

ex_en: He's in debt to the bank.
note: f. مديونة madyūna.

note: pl. قمم gimam. Also a "summit" meeting.

ex_en: Next week we'll go out to the countryside.
note: Very Libyan: طلعنا للبر = we went out to the countryside/desert for a picnic or camping trip.

ex_en: The car broke down on us in the middle of nowhere.
note: في الخلا = out in the middle of nowhere.

phrases.en: there's nobody out in the wilds

ex_en: My grandfather lives in the countryside.

phrases.en: from the countryside to the city

ex_en: The view from the mountain top is amazing.
note: pl. مناظر manāDHir.

ex_ar: الشط هذا كله حصى مش رملة.
ex_en: This beach is all pebbles, not sand.
note: Singular حصاية 7Sāya (a pebble).

ex_en: The rain left puddles on the road.
note: pl. برك birak. Different from بركة baraka "blessing".

ex_en: The ring fell to the bottom of the sea.

ex_ar: فيه نسمة باردة جاية من البحر.
ex_tr: fīh nisma bārda jāya min il-ba7ar.
ex_en: There's a cool breeze coming from the sea.
note: Also used for a "soul/person" in counts (عدد النسمات).

ex_en: There's a dark cloud coming.
note: pl. غيوم ghyūm; collective غيم ghēm. سحاب is also used.

ex_en: A strong storm came yesterday.
note: pl. عواصف 3wāSif. عاصفة رملية = sandstorm.

ex_en: The sea is rough, there's a storm.
note: Libyan/Maghrebi word for a spell of stormy, rainy weather.

phrases.en: the fishermen didn't go out because of the storm

ex_en: In the morning the car is covered in dew.
note: Also a girl's name.

phrases.en: the grass is wet with dew

ex_en: It's freezing tonight, dress well.
note: Maghrebi word for biting cold; الدنيا صقع = it's freezing.

ex_en: Hail fell and broke the glass.
note: Maghrebi word; MSA برَد barad.

ex_en: It's not rain, just a bit of drizzle.
After the rain a rainbow appeared.
The flood came down the wadi yesterday.
note: pl. سيول syūl. The wadis fill with sēl after heavy rain.

ex_en: The flood destroyed half the town.
note: pl. فيضانات fayaDānāt. Libyans remember فيضان درنة (Derna flood, 2023).

ex_ar: السنة هذي فيها جفاف، ما صبتش.
ex_tr: is-sana hādhi fīha jafāf, ma Sabbatsh.
ex_en: This year there's a drought, it hasn't rained.
The earthquake happened at night.
note: pl. زلازل zalāzil.

ex_en: Haruj mountain has old volcanoes.
note: pl. براكين barākīn.

phrases.en: like a volcano (about an angry person)

ex_en: Libya's climate is hot and dry.
Did you see the forecast? It'll rain tomorrow.
We go to the sea before sunrise.
note: شروق الشمس.

ex_en: Sunset over the sea is gorgeous.
note: غروب الشمس.

ex_en: The ship appeared on the horizon.
note: pl. آفاق āfāg (also "prospects").

ex_ar: في الصحرا تشوف سراب كأنه مية.
ex_en: In the desert you see a mirage like water.
Tonight the moon is full.
note: Also a man's name. وجهها زي البدر = her face is like the full moon.

phrases.en: the night of the full moon

ex_ar: صار كسوف في الشمس العام اللي فات.
ex_tr: Sār ksūf fish-shams il-3ām illi fāt.
ex_en: There was a solar eclipse last year.
note: Lunar eclipse = خسوف khsūf.

phrases.en: don't look at the eclipse with your bare eyes

ex_en: Tonight there's a lunar eclipse.
note: Solar eclipse = كسوف ksūf.

ex_en: The Earth is a planet, and the sun is a star.
note: pl. كواكب kawākib.

ex_en: My son wants to become an astronaut.
It's dark, turn on the light.
note: الدنيا ضلمة = it's dark.

ex_en: Not a single drop of rain fell.
note: pl. قطرات gaTrāt. Also eye drops (قطرة للعين).

ex_en: Steam is coming out of the pot.
The olive season starts in autumn.
note: pl. مواسم mawāsim. فصل is a season of the year; موسم is a harvest/activity season.

ex_en: There was a fire in the forest.
note: pl. حرايق 7rāyig. نار is fire in general; حريق is a destructive fire.

phrases.en: the fire brigade came to the fire

ex_en: Tea made on embers is tastier.
note: Singular جمرة jamra.

ex_ar: بعد الشوي ما بقى غير الرماد.
ex_tr: ba3d ish-shwi ma bga ghēr ir-rmād.
ex_en: After the barbecue only ash was left.
The lighthouse shines for ships at night.
note: pl. منارات manārāt.

ex_en: Don't swim far, the current is strong.
note: Also electric current (تيار كهربا) and a political "trend".

ex_en: The tide came in and the beach got narrow.
note: المد والجزر = the tides.

ex_en: At low tide the rocks show.
note: Same spelling as جزر jazar "carrots". The Mediterranean tide is small.

ex_en: A big wave came and soaked us.
note: pl. مواج mwāj; collective موج. موجة حر = a heat wave.

ex_en: My brother loves fishing with a rod.
note: صيد الحوت = fishing; صيد الغزال = hunting gazelle.

ex_en: The fishermen are mending the nets.
note: pl. شباك shbāk. Also means a phone/internet network.

ex_ar: شريت صنارة جديدة من سوق الحوت.
ex_tr: shrēt Sannāra jdīda min sūg il-7ūt.
ex_en: I bought a new fishing rod at the fish market.
note: pl. صنانير Sanānīr.

ex_en: Put the bait on the hook.
note: Different from طعم Ta3m "taste".

phrases.en: the fish didn't take the bait

ex_en: We got into a small boat.
note: pl. قوارب gawārib. فلوكة is the usual word for a small fishing boat.

ex_en: The boat went out to sea at dawn.
note: pl. مراكب marākib.

ex_en: The coast guard came in the launch.
note: From English "launch". pl. لنشات lanshāt.

ex_en: The wind pushed the sail.
note: pl. أشرعة ashri3a.

ex_en: Row with the oar to the shore.
note: pl. مجاديف mjādīf.

ex_en: They dropped anchor near the shore.
note: Fishermen also say أنكرة ankra (from Italian ancora).

ex_ar: البنات يلمّوا في الصدف على الشط.
ex_en: The girls are collecting shells on the beach.
note: pl. صدف Sdaf. Same spelling as صدفة "coincidence".

ex_en: Clams are eaten raw with lemon.
note: Collective; one = محارة ma7āra.

ex_ar: الورقة غالية اليوم في سوق الحوت.
ex_tr: il-warga ghālya il-yōm fi sūg il-7ūt.
ex_en: Sea bream is expensive today at the fish market.
note: Libyan fish-market name for dorade/sea bream; same word as ورقة "leaf/paper".

ex_en: Mullet is cheap and eaten in 7rāymi.
Salema is a cheap fish full of bones.
note: Common cheap Mediterranean fish in Libyan markets.

ex_en: There's red coral under the sea.
note: Also the name of a reddish sea bream at the fish market, and a girl's name.

ex_en: Grouper is a big fish with white flesh.
note: Fish-market loanword (Spanish/Italian mero).

ex_en: They said they saw a shark near the beach.
note: Also حوت القرش. Same spelling as قرش "a piece of money".

ex_en: We saw dolphins behind the boat.
note: pl. دلافين dalāfīn.

ex_ar: انتبه، فيه قنديل بحر في المية.
ex_en: Watch out, there's a jellyfish in the water.
note: Also called ميدوزا mēdūza.

ex_en: He brought her a pearl necklace for the wedding.
note: One pearl = لؤلؤة lūlūwa.

ex_en: This door is made of iron.
Gold got very expensive this year.
note: Libyans also say ذهب for gold jewellery in general.

phrases.en: he has a heart of gold

ex_en: This anklet is old Libyan silver.
This tray is pure copper.
note: سوق النحاس / سوق الصياغة in Tripoli old city.

ex_en: We heard gunfire last night.
note: Also bullets; رصاص حي = live rounds.

ex_en: Wrap the fish in tinfoil.
note: Also tinfoil (ورق قصدير).

ex_en: This cup is metal, not plastic.
note: pl. معادن ma3ādin.

ex_en: This table is made of olive wood.
note: pl. أخشاب akhshāb.

ex_en: We gathered firewood to light the fire.
Meat over charcoal comes out tasty.
Libya lives off oil.
note: The formal word; in speech also بترول bitrōl. مؤسسة النفط = the National Oil Corporation.

ex_ar: بابا يخدم في شركة بترول في الصحرا.
ex_tr: bāba yikhdim fi shirkat bitrōl fiS-Sa7ra.
ex_en: Dad works for an oil company in the desert.
note: Everyday synonym of نفط. Petrol for the car is بنزينة banzīna.

ex_en: They shut the oil field because of the troubles.
note: pl. حقول 7gūl. In Libya mostly heard as حقل نفط.

ex_en: The Zawiya refinery is stopped today.
note: مصفاة الزاوية = Zawiya refinery.

ex_en: There's an iron mine in the south.
note: pl. مناجم manājim.

ex_en: They whitewashed the wall with lime.
note: Houses in old Libyan towns were whitewashed with جير.

ex_en: In the old days they coated camels with tar.
note: Traditionally used on camel skin and to waterproof water skins.

ex_ar: ملح البحر أصح من الملح العادي.
ex_tr: mil7 il-ba7ar aSa77 min il-mil7 il-3ādi.
ex_en: Sea salt is healthier than ordinary salt.
note: Libya also harvests salt from sabkhas (salt flats).

ex_en: We spend Friday at my grandfather's farm.
note: Very Libyan word for a family farm or orchard, traditionally irrigated from a well. pl. سواني swāni.

phrases.en: he has a farm in Tajoura

ex_en: The farm has cows and chickens.
note: pl. مزارع mazāri3. Used for bigger or commercial farms; سانية is the homely word.

ex_ar: جدي عاش عمره كله في الفلاحة.
ex_en: My grandfather spent his whole life farming.
note: Everyday word for farm work. أرض فلاحية = farmland.

ex_ar: الزراعة في الجنوب تحتاج مية هلبة.
ex_en: Farming in the south needs a lot of water.
note: وزارة الزراعة = Ministry of Agriculture.

ex_en: The crop is good this year.
note: pl. محاصيل ma7āSīl.

ex_en: The olive harvest this year is huge.
note: Maghrebi word: الصابة باهية = the harvest is good.

ex_ar: الجمعة الجاية جنية الزيتون في السانية.
ex_en: Next week is the olive picking at the farm.
note: جنية الزيتون = the olive harvest, when families gather to pick.

ex_en: The harvest is in summer.
We took the olives to the press.
note: pl. معاصر ma3āSir. Families take their olives to the ma3Sra after picking.

phrases.en: the queue at the olive press

ex_ar: السانية تحتاج ري كل يوم في الصيف.
ex_tr: is-sānya ti7tāj rayy kull yōm fiS-Sēf.
ex_en: The farm needs irrigating every day in summer.
The water runs through the channel to the trees.
note: pl. سواقي swāgi.

ex_en: The kids swim in the irrigation basin.
note: Open masonry basin on a سانية that stores well water for irrigation.

ex_en: The sheep drink from the trough.
note: pl. أحواض a7wāD. Also a sink basin or a fish tank (حوض حوت).

ex_en: The pump is broken, there's no water.
note: From Italian tromba. Also موتور الماء.

ex_en: We installed drip irrigation for the olives.
note: ري بالتنقيط.

ex_en: We put the seeds in the soil.
note: pl. بذور bdhūr. Also زريعة zrī3a for seeds to sow.

ex_en: He bought watermelon seed at the market.
note: Maghrebi collective for seed. (Roasted snack seeds are usually قلوب.)

ex_en: We planted twenty olive saplings.
note: pl. شتلات shatlāt / شتول shtūl.

ex_en: Put fertiliser on the tomatoes so they grow.
note: Also مخصب. Natural manure is زبل zibl.

ex_en: Sheep manure is good for the soil.
note: On the farm it means manure; in town it can also mean rubbish/garbage.

ex_en: In the past they ploughed with a plough and a mule.
note: pl. محاريث m7ārīth.

ex_en: Ploughing comes after the first rain.
note: Verb حرث 7rath, imperfect يحرث yi7rith.

ex_en: Take the hoe and dig around the tree.
note: pl. فيسان fīsān. The basic Libyan farm tool for digging.

ex_en: He reaped the barley with a sickle.
note: pl. مناجل mnājil.

ex_en: He opened the channel with the spade.
note: Used to move earth and open irrigation channels.

ex_en: Olive trees need pruning every year.
They built the pen from palm fronds.
note: One = جريدة jrīda. Used for fences, baskets and roofing.

ex_en: The palm has ten date bunches.
note: pl. عراجين 3arājīn.

ex_en: In the past they made ropes from palm fibre.
note: Palm fibre used for ropes; also a bath scrubber (ليفة līfa).

ex_en: We sat under the grapevine in the courtyard.
note: pl. دوالي dwāli. Many Tripoli courtyards have a dālya for shade.

ex_en: The ears have turned yellow; harvest is near.
note: pl. سنابل snābil.

ex_en: Put out some straw for the animals.
Fodder went up and so did sheep.
note: Price of علف is a big topic for Libyan livestock owners.

ex_en: We planted clover for the cows.
note: Also called فصة fiSSa.

ex_en: Put the sheep back in the pen.
note: pl. زرايب zrāyib.

ex_en: The hens sleep in the coop.
The horses are in the stable.
note: pl. إسطبلات isTablāt.

ex_en: Spring has come and the pasture is good.
note: pl. مراعي marā3i.

ex_en: The kids go out herding with the sheep.
note: Verb رعى ra3a, imperfect يرعى yir3a.

ex_en: He has a big flock of sheep.
note: pl. قطعان giT3ān.

ex_en: This blanket is pure wool.
This wrap is made of camel hair.
Libya imports grain from abroad.
note: Same word means pills/tablets in a health context.

ex_en: The wadi is full of reeds.
note: قصب السكر = sugar cane.

ex_en: Do you have a pet at home?
note: pl. حيوانات أليفة.

ex_en: My grandfather has livestock on the farm.
note: Singular بهيمة bhīma. Used as an insult too (يا بهيمة = you dumb animal).

ex_en: Livestock prices are rising before Eid.
note: Formal/news word; at home people say بهايم or غنم.

ex_en: My uncle works in beekeeping.
note: تربية الدجاج = poultry farming; in people, "upbringing/manners".

ex_en: Put the saddle on the horse.
note: pl. سروج srūj. The decorated Libyan saddle is used at fantasia shows.

ex_en: He pulled the reins and the horse stopped.
The bird in the cage is singing.
note: pl. أقفاص agfāS. Also a crate of fruit/veg.

ex_en: We set a trap for the mouse.
note: pl. فخاخ fkhākh. Also figuratively: طاح في الفخ = he fell into the trap.

ex_en: There's a pigeon nest above the window.
note: pl. عشوش 3shūsh.

ex_ar: عنده عشر خلايا نحل في الجبل.
ex_en: He has ten beehives in the mountains.
note: pl. خلايا khalāya. Also a (biological or militant) cell.

ex_en: The cow gave birth to a calf yesterday.
note: pl. عجول 3jūl. Also لحم عجل = veal.

ex_en: This bull is very strong.
note: pl. ثيران thīrān.

ex_en: The goat had two kids.
note: pl. جديان jidyān. Same spelling as جدي jiddi "serious".

ex_en: The billy goat has long horns.
note: pl. تيوس tyūs. Also an insult for a stubborn person.

phrases.en: a billy goat and ten nanny goats

ex_en: We bought a lamb for Eid.
note: pl. خرفان khirfān. In Libya علوش is the common word; خروف is pan-Arabic.

ex_en: This year we bought a fat yearling sheep.
note: A sheep in its second year, the preferred age for the Eid sacrifice. Same word as the حولي wrap (clothing).

ex_en: The mare had a white foal.
note: Female مهرة muhra. Not the same as مهر mahr "dowry".

phrases.en: the foal runs after its mother

ex_en: The ducks swim in the pond.
note: Collective بط baTT.

ex_ar: الوز يصيّح لو يجي حد غريب.
ex_en: The geese honk if a stranger comes.
note: Collective وز wizz.

ex_en: We bought a turkey for the dinner party.
The hen hatched ten chicks.
note: pl. فراخ frākh. Also used for the young of other animals.

ex_ar: عنده مية راس بل في الجنوب.
ex_en: He has a hundred head of camels in the south.
note: Libyans say البل il-bil. Singular جمل/ناقة.

ex_en: There are wild boars in the forest.
note: Maghrebi word; MSA خنزير khanzīr. Also a strong insult.

ex_en: Muslims don't eat pork.
note: pl. خنازير khanāzīr. Everyday Libyan also حلّوف.

ex_en: We saw a bear at the zoo.
note: pl. دببة dibaba.

ex_en: Is the tiger faster than the lion?
note: pl. نمور nmūr.

ex_en: The kids love to see the elephant.
note: pl. فيلة fiyala / فيلان fīlān.

ex_en: The monkey is eating bananas.
note: pl. قرود grūd. Also a playful insult for a naughty child.

ex_en: The giraffe has a long neck.
The fox ate the hen.
note: pl. ثعالب tha3ālib. Also a cunning person.

ex_ar: زمان يقولوا فيه ضباع في الجبل.
ex_en: In the past they said there were hyenas in the mountains.
note: pl. ضباع Dbā3.

ex_en: We found a hedgehog on the farm.
note: Maghrebi form; MSA قنفذ.

phrases.en: the hedgehog rolls into a ball

ex_en: The Barbary sheep lives in the desert mountains.
note: Wild mountain sheep of the Libyan Sahara; a symbol of the town of Waddan and of Libyan wildlife.

ex_en: The jerboa hops like a kangaroo.
note: pl. يرابيع yarābī3. Small hopping desert rodent.

ex_ar: الصغير يخاف من الوحوش في الليل.
ex_en: The little one is scared of monsters at night.
note: pl. وحوش w7ūsh. Slang: وحش = a beast (impressive person/thing).

ex_en: The dab lizard lives in the desert.
note: Large desert lizard; some Bedouin eat it.

ex_en: The monitor lizard is almost a metre long.
note: pl. ورلان warlān.

ex_ar: فيه بوبريص على الحيط في الكوجينة.
ex_en: There's a gecko on the kitchen wall.
note: From أبو بريص. The little gecko seen on walls at night.

ex_en: The lizard ran between the stones.
note: Maghrebi word for the small ground lizard. MSA سحلية.

ex_en: The chameleon changes its colour.
note: Also figuratively a two-faced person.

ex_en: The crocodile lives in the Nile.
note: pl. تماسيح tamāsī7.

ex_ar: الجران يغنوا في الليل في الساقية.
ex_en: The frogs croak at night in the channel.
note: Maghrebi word; MSA ضفدع Dafda3. pl. جران jrān.

ex_en: Careful, there's a viper under the stone.
note: Libyan/Maghrebi form of أفعى; حنش is a snake in general.

ex_en: Bats come out at night.
note: pl. خفافيش khafāfīsh.

ex_en: The owl hoots at night.
note: Seen as a bad omen by some people.

ex_en: The eagle is flying above the mountain.
note: pl. نسور nsūr.

ex_en: The falcon caught a pigeon.
note: pl. صقور Sgūr. Falconry (الصيد بالصقور) is practised in the Libyan desert.

ex_en: The crow is standing on the pole.
note: pl. غربان ghirbān. Considered a bad omen.

ex_en: The birds sing early in the morning.
note: pl. عصافير 3aSāfīr.

phrases.en: killed two birds with one stone

ex_en: The starlings came with the winter.
note: pl. زرازير zarāzīr. Large flocks come in winter.

ex_en: They hunted partridges in the mountains.
note: pl. حجل 7jal.

phrases.en: she walks gracefully like a partridge

ex_en: The quail come in autumn.
note: Migrating quail pass the Libyan coast in autumn.

ex_en: The turtle dove built a nest in the vine.
note: pl. يمام ymām.

ex_en: The parrot can say hello.
note: Also used for someone who repeats without understanding.

ex_en: The ostrich egg is very big.
note: pl. نعام n3ām.

phrases.en: like an ostrich (head in the sand)

ex_en: Our neighbour has a canary that sings.
Seagulls are flying over the port.
note: pl. نوارس nawāris.

ex_en: The nightingale sings in the tree.
note: Also said of someone who speaks a language fluently (يتكلم زي البلبل).

ex_en: I saw a hoopoe on the farm.
note: Known from the Quran story of Solomon.

ex_en: The peacock spread its feathers.
note: Also said of a vain person.

ex_en: The houbara comes to the desert in winter.
note: Desert bird hunted with falcons.

ex_en: The saluki runs faster than a hare.
note: Lean hunting dog of the Bedouin.

ex_en: The dog had five puppies.
note: Also a harsh insult for a woman.

ex_en: The cat had little kittens.
note: Masc. قطوس gaTTūs.

ex_en: The buffalo gives a lot of milk.
note: Collective جاموس jāmūs.

ex_en: The zebra is striped black and white.
The cheetah is the fastest animal.
note: Also a man's name.

ex_en: The squirrel climbed up the tree.

ex_ar: الحوت الكبير أكبر حيوان في الدنيا.
ex_en: The whale is the biggest animal in the world.
note: Since حوت alone means "fish" in Libya, a whale is حوت كبير or حوت أزرق.

ex_en: The sea turtle lays eggs in the sand.
note: Loggerhead turtles nest on Libyan beaches. On land, a tortoise is فكرون.

ex_en: Wildlife has become scarce in Libya.
note: برّي = wild (vs. tame/domestic).

ex_en: We took the kids to the zoo.
note: Tripoli zoo is in أبو سليم.

ex_en: The house is full of insects in summer.
note: pl. حشرات 7asharāt.

ex_en: The butterflies in spring are colourful.
note: pl. فراشات farāshāt.

ex_en: The locusts ate all the crops.
note: Collective جراد jrād. Locust swarms sometimes hit southern Libya.

ex_en: The dog has fleas.
note: pl. براغيث barāghīth.

ex_en: She brought lice home from school.
note: Collective قمل gmal. Lice in school kids' hair is a common worry.

ex_en: There's a spider in the corner of the room.
note: pl. عناكب 3anākib.

ex_en: The apple has a worm in it.
note: Collective دود dūd.

ex_en: The hotel had bedbugs.
note: Collective بق bagg.

ex_en: A wasp stung me on the hand.
note: pl. دبابير dbābīr.

ex_en: A black beetle is walking on the floor.
note: pl. خنافس khnāfis.

ex_en: After the rain the snails came out.
note: After rain the snails come out on the farm.

phrases.en: he moves at a snail's pace

ex_en: A tick got stuck on the dog.
note: Collective قراد grād.

ex_en: The caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
note: pl. يرقات yargāt.

ex_en: The pillow is stuffed with feathers.
note: One = ريشة rīsha (also a pen nib or paintbrush). Same word means lamb chops at the butcher's.

ex_en: The bird's wing is broken.
note: pl. جوانح jwāni7 (also chicken wings as food) / أجنحة.

ex_en: The bird pecked with its beak.
note: pl. مناقير mnāgīr.

ex_en: The dog is wagging its tail.
